rows.description: Someone makes a snide remark about my food or dress. I feel small and angry. Wise: answer calmly or walk away, seek allies, and stay proud of my background. Harmful: withdrawing into resentment.

rows.description: I did what I was supposed to do, and now I wonder what it is all for. Wise: try small experiments, meet people, help someone, and let purpose emerge from action rather than being found. Harmful: numbing with scrolling.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, curiosity, envy, worship
related mind states: curiosity, detachment, awe

rows.description: My parents' dream for me is not mine, and I feel like a fraud pursuing it. Wise: tell them what I actually love, propose a path with a fallback, and accept their worry. Harmful: silent compliance or dramatic rebellion.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, curiosity, envy, worship

rows.description: My friends seem to know what they want, and I feel behind. Wise: most people are guessing; social media hides it. Try things and follow what holds my interest. Harmful: comparing my confusion to their highlights.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, curiosity, worship
related mind states: interest, confusion, envy

rows.description: I ask an older person how she found her direction and she says she changed course three times. Wise: collect stories, not formulas; direction often forms while walking. Harmful: waiting for certainty.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, envy, worship

rows.description: I turn to a book, tradition or practice to find meaning. Wise: let it challenge and comfort me, discuss with others. Harmful: adopting a ready-made answer that spares me from thinking.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, curiosity, envy

rows.description: I call myself lazy and directionless and think I have wasted my youth. Wise: stagnation is often exhaustion, fear or depression; be kind, take one tiny step, seek help if it persists. Harmful: harsh labels as a way to feel in control.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, envy, worship
related mind states: contempt, fear, tiredness

rows.description: After a serious mistake I hear a voice saying "you are worthless". Wise: separate what I did from who I am, own the harm, repair it, and speak to myself as I would to a friend. Harmful: hiding it or self-punishment.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, compassion, disillusionment, forgiveness, pride

rows.description: I learn to say "I made a mistake, and I am still a person worth respect". Wise: self-compassion makes accountability easier, not weaker. Harmful: using kindness to excuse repeating the harm.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, disillusionment, forgiveness, pride, shame

rows.description: The person I hurt says she forgives me. I feel relief and do not feel worthy. Wise: accept it humbly, change behaviour, and do not demand more from her. Harmful: treating forgiveness as a reset with no effort.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, compassion, disillusionment, pride, shame
